card.name: Modifiers before a clinical condition term
card.fires_on: Adjectives or articles such as chronic, high, and a that come right before a condition or state noun (migraine, risk, airway, euthyroid state). Also seen on cancers and the end of a drug name.

modes.label: Chronic or high before condition
modes.description: The word chronic or high sits before a disease or dose term, often after For or with.
modes.example: For<< chronic>> migraine, concomitant use of strong

modes.label: A before a medical state
modes.description: The article a comes before a clinical state or object after verbs like maintain or receive.
modes.example: used to maintain<< a>> euthyroid state.

modes.label: Disease or drug name ending
modes.description: The last part of a noun naming a cancer type or a branded drug.
modes.example: approximately one-third of human breast<< cancers>> are prolactin-dependent in vitro ,

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward words like constit, presenting, screen and panel that start a following term.
card.plain: It fires on small describing words just before a condition or clinical state is named.
